top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a discovery with a clear conceptual origin (the Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and time-reversal-protected helical edge states) and a decisive measurement (quantised edge conductance in HgTe wells), confirmed for about two decades by independent probes and carried into photonic, mechanical and cold-atom systems. Z2 matter without a magnetic field is distinct from the quantum Hall and defect-transition topology recognised in 2016. The weakness is real: Molenkamp tested the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and not the graphene model, so the citation must be confined to the Z2 state and its first observation in HgTe and must not imply credit for BHZ or the 3D topological insulators. I judge that a bounded, honest wording keeps P001 ahead of P002, whose direct theory-to-experiment chain is cleaner but whose pairing mechanism is still unsettled after about seven years. P003 has the cleanest two-name credit but follows earlier precision-measurement prizes, and Katori's priority rests on history I cannot verify. All three beat no award.
